newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta index ends up on blue-chips, speculation.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta index ends up on blue-chips, speculation.

text.p: Speculative buying of second-liners and improved sentiment on selected blue chips gave further gains to the Jakarta index on Wednesday, brokers said.

The Jakarta composite index rose 2.07 points, or 0.31 percent, to close at 659.35 points. Turn-over was 467.62 billion rupiah compared with 336.27 billion rupiah on Tuesday. Decliners matched advancers by 57 to 57 with 65 issues unchanged.
"Focus remains on selected big-caps like Telkom and some small-caps such as Modern Land," one broker said.
Brokers said the U.S. Fed's decision to raise key interest rates did not have much impact on the market as it had already been discounted and the focus was more on local issues.
Telkom remained among the most actively traded issues, up 75 rupiah to close at 3,650 after rising 25 rupiah on Tuesday.

"At its current price levels, Telkom still remains attractive especially among the rising number of local fund management firms. Because Telkom is a must despite all the rumours about a possible competitor," an analyst with a foreign brokerage firm said.
He said local appetite for Telkom had helped it to stage a modest rebound despite sustained foreign selling pressure.

"It would be impossible for the government to end Telkom's monopoly ahead of schedule as it would draw sharp reactions after all those issues like the Busang gold find, national car issue and also ahead of the general election," the analyst said.
Telkom shares in Jakarta, London and New York were under pressure last week after reports that a possible competitor link to President Suharto's brother-in-law Sudwikatmono would emerge.
Telkom denied the rumours, saying a government regulation granting it monopoly over local calls until 2011 and domestic inter-city calls until 2006 was still effective.
Second-liner Modern Land was the most actively traded issue, closing 775 rupiah higher at 2,650 rupiah.
Brokers attributed the sharp rise to a possible link-up with a Japanese property firm, but the firm denied the rumour.

"The buying is rather speculative. It's nothing unusual. We have often seen stocks rising almost 50 percent in active trading in one day because on speculation and than falling sharply the next day for unknown reasons," the broker said.
Heavyweight cigarette maker Sampoerna closed 325 rupiah higher at 11,500 rupiah.
"It's a technical rebound, but it is unlikely to continue for long. It may touch the 12,000 level but it is unlikely to go back to its 1997 high of 15,150 rupiah in February," one analyst said.
He said new regulations on cigarettes including a requirement to allocate 10 percent of sales profits to distributors was expected to cap any possible surprises on its 1997 net profit.
